note: Matches the profile on paper and fails on all three criteria that decide anything. Successful: he owns a cleaning business, which is literally the business-owner case the stated ICP names. Not_deconditioned: he clears the exclusion comfortably — trains, has held one-minute handstands, has done CrossFit and 100 pull-ups in a session, and is nowhere near 50 lb overweight or gym-averse. Income is a clear miss: "I am downsized in my business and I cannot afford it", he had no price expectation at all and had never bought coaching of any kind. Neglected_health is a miss in the opposite direction from the usual — health is not the neglected area of his life, it is the area he has worked on continuously since 50, and what he actually presents with is active chronic disease: a single kidney with a protein restriction, rheumatoid arthritis with measurable six-month decline, and a recent depressive episode. That is a crisis-adjacent medical picture, not a neglected one. Good_to_great is a miss: he is climbing back out of a six-month collapse, in his own words "I couldn't get up the hole", which is rescue. Recorded as outside rather than edge because three of five criteria fail and they are the three that determine whether the programme can serve or be paid by him. The pattern worth carrying to the rollup is the same one the ICP file already flags: there is no clinical criterion, so a 63-year-old with one kidney and inflammatory arthritis reads as an ICP match on occupation and starting point right up until the nutrition advice and the load-progression guarantee collide with his actual body.
